notebook.title: A notebook of small things
notebook.text: {person} shows you sketches of ordinary things: a chipped cup, a bent gate, the view from a window. They want to make a small book. "I want time for this, even if it never earns anything."

choices.label: Ask what kind of support would help
choices.result: I listened to {person} describe the book. I offered to look at an early page, without promising to manage the project.

choices.label: Offer materials with no conditions
choices.result: {person} accepted my help with paper and materials. The money came without a claim on the book or a promise to work together.

choices.label: Leave the project in their hands
choices.result: I made no commitment to join in. {person} kept the notebook and the right to continue without me.

choices.label: Ask them to make it pay before I help
choices.result: I made my help conditional on income. {person} said the book did not need to become another bill to meet.

first_attempt.title: An uneven first page
first_attempt.text: The first pages have rubbed-out lines and an awkward fold. {person} likes one drawing enough to keep going. They ask whether you still want to look at a page together, without taking charge.

choices.label: Offer one evening, if they still want that
choices.result: I offered one evening to look at the pages. {person} kept the decision about whether to share that time.

choices.label: Offer practical costs without joining
choices.result: {person} accepted help with copying costs. I did not turn that help into a seat at the drawing table.

choices.label: Make no further commitment
choices.result: I left the next attempt to {person}. My earlier involvement did not oblige either of us to continue together.

own_terms.title: A project with its own pace
own_terms.text: {person} has kept a few pages and discarded others. They want the work to stay theirs. Your time together matters, but it need not include every pursuit.

choices.label: Respect separate pursuits
choices.result: I accepted that {person} could keep this part of life separate. There was room for my interests too.

choices.label: Ask whether a small shared part would suit them
choices.result: I asked about sharing a small part of the work, leaving {person} free to refuse.

choices.label: Make my support conditional on more involvement
choices.result: I said support should mean more involvement for me. {person} would not exchange control of the book for my approval.

refusal.title: Their answer is no
refusal.text: {person} declines a joint arrangement. They are continuing the book independently. "You can care about me without being part of this." An apology may matter, but it is not a new agreement.

choices.label: Acknowledge the pressure I put on them
choices.result: I acknowledged the pressure I had put on {person}. I did not ask them to reward the apology by letting me back into the project.

choices.label: Leave the refusal in place
choices.result: I left {person}'s refusal in place. They could continue without another negotiation.

choices.label: Keep insisting that support earns a say
choices.result: I kept treating support as a claim on {person}'s work. They refused that claim. The disagreement remained; no shared arrangement followed.

shared_close.title: A small place beside them
shared_close.text: {person} has chosen to share a small part of the work with you. Some pages remain private. The book still has no earnings target, and neither of you owes the other a permanent role.

choices.label: Keep the invitation small and voluntary
choices.result: I accepted the small invitation {person} offered. We kept room to change our minds, and the book remained theirs.

choices.label: Choose separate pursuits from here
choices.result: I stepped back from the shared part. {person} kept working, and I made room for pursuits of my own.
choices.outcome: Two pursuits with room to grow

choices.label: Let the invitation lapse
choices.result: I made no new commitment. The shared invitation lapsed without giving me a claim on what {person} made next.

parallel_close.title: Two unfinished futures
parallel_close.text: {person} is still making pages at their own pace. Some may never leave the notebook. Your part in this story does not have to be a shared project.

choices.label: Leave room for both lives
choices.result: I left room for {person}'s work and for interests of my own. Separate pursuits did not make either life less important.
choices.outcome: Two pursuits with room to grow

choices.label: Name what I learned about control
choices.result: I named the difference between helping and claiming a say. {person}'s independent work did not need my permission.

choices.label: Keep my reflection private
choices.result: I kept my reflection on {person}'s project private. I did not leave this story as instructions for the next generation.

separation.title: After the partnership
separation.text: Your partnership with {person} has ended elsewhere in your life. The notebook is still theirs. Past help creates no right to their time, their pages, or a renewed relationship.

choices.label: Let the unfinished arrangement end
choices.result: My partnership with {person} had ended. I let the unfinished arrangement end too, without treating earlier help as a debt.
choices.outcome: An ended partnership, not an unpaid debt

choices.label: Keep the lesson without seeking a reunion
choices.result: I kept what I learned from {person}'s plans. That memory was not a request to resume our partnership.

loss.title: The pages left unfinished
loss.text: {lost_person} has died. The plans you discussed cannot become a new agreement now. You can remember the person without inventing an ending for their work.

choices.label: Remember the person and the unfinished work
choices.result: I remembered {lost_person} and the work they wanted time for. I did not turn the unfinished pages into a duty for someone else.
choices.outcome: A person remembered beyond the project

choices.label: Keep the memory private
choices.result: I kept my memory of {lost_person}'s unfinished work private. No one else had to finish it for me.

pages.title: A life alongside another
pages.text: You read the public record of your parent's story with {person}. The outcome below belongs to that life, not to a perfect example of partnership. You can keep the memory without inheriting its arrangement.

choices.label: Adapt the lesson to my own life
choices.result: I read my parent's account of {person}'s plans. I kept the lesson of asking what support means, while leaving my own arrangements open.

choices.label: Preserve the story without adopting it
choices.result: I preserved my parent's account of {person}. Remembering their choices did not require me to build the same life.

choices.label: Put down the obligation
choices.result: I put down the idea that my parent's story with {person} was an obligation. Their record remained intact; my choices were still mine.
